newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Nigeria's Abacha visits Ivory Coast.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's Abacha visits Ivory Coast.

text.p: Nigeria's military ruler General Sani Abacha arrived in Abidjan on Monday for a one-day "working and friendship visit" to Ivory Coast, officials said.
The visit had not been previously announced and Nigerian officials said Abacha, chairman of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), was expected to go on to Guinea.
Nigeria, Ivory Coast, Guinea and Ghana are members of a special committee of the 16-nation ECOWAS dealing with a crisis created by a military coup in Sierra Leone on May 25.

Nigeria leads the community's military wing, whose troops are confronting the coup leaders in Freetown and enforcing an ECOWAS economic embargo on the country to force the restoration of ousted civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
Kabbah is exiled in Guinea, which borders Sierra Leone.
The United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity have condemned the coup and demanded the reinstatement of Kabbah, toppled just over a year after his election.

Talks between foreign ministers of the special committee and envoys of the Freetown government broke down last month in Abidjan last month after junta leader Johnny Paul Koroma announced he would retain power until 2001.
ECOWAS ordered sanctions stepped up and Nigerian troops clashed last week at Freetown airport with Sierra Leone army soldiers backed by former rebels who rallied to the coup.
The foreign ministers ended talks in the Ghanaian capital Accra at the weekend to decide the next line of action.
Abacha was received by Ivorian President Henri Konan Bedie and the two held a first meeting at the airport lounge without aides, Ivorian officials said.
They then drove into town for further talks at Bedie's office.
